beats.care: If you or your family have a floating-rate home, car or education loan, EMIs can rise. On ₹30 lakh, that's roughly ₹480 a month.
beats.what: From 15 October, SBI raised its repo-linked lending rate from 7.50% to 7.75%, and several MCLR rates by 0.15 points.
beats.why: RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50% on 7 October to fight rising prices. Banks pass that higher cost on to borrowers.

cards.body: It was 7.50%. Your actual loan rate is this plus a small risk premium the bank adds.
cards.caption: SBI's new repo-linked lending rate

cards.body: SBI isn't alone. Right after RBI's hike, PNB, Bank of Baroda, Indian Bank, Bank of India and Indian Overseas Bank also raised their repo-linked rates by 0.25 points.
Only on floating-rate loans. Repo-linked loans reset fastest; MCLR loans change at your reset date. Fixed-rate loans don't change. Some banks stretch the loan's length instead of raising the EMI.
cards.title: will my emi change automatically?

cards.body: Loans got costlier, but SBI left its fixed deposit rates unchanged in this revision. Borrowers pay more; savers don't earn more, yet.

cards.q: Would a higher EMI change your plans?
Why did SBI raise its loan rates?
cards.why: When RBI makes borrowing costlier for banks, banks pass it on to you through loan rates.

hook: RBI hiked rates. Now *SBI's loans cost more*. How much more for you?

learn.t: Since 2019, new floating-rate home loans must track an outside benchmark, usually RBI's repo rate, so hikes reach EMIs within weeks.

tldr: SBI raised its loan benchmark rates by up to 0.25 points from 15 October, passing on RBI's rate hike, so many floating-rate EMIs will rise.
watch: October's retail inflation data is due in mid-November. If prices keep rising, RBI could hike again and EMIs could climb further.
